headline: 30-hour blockade: CUET VC rescued from administrative building by DC and SP
summary: Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Islam was freed after being locked inside his office by protesting students demanding his resignation.
details: Chattogram's deputy commissioner, superintendent of police, and the CUET proctor rescued Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Islam after he was confined for nearly 30 hours.
The situation began yesterday when demonstrating students locked the VC inside the administrative building around 12:30 PM, demanding his immediate resignation.
The confrontation flared up yesterday morning when the VC arrived on campus for the first time since his September 21 appointment, entering through the main gate by identifying himself as a teacher.
Students gathered in hundreds, chanting slogans and rejecting the new VC. They gave him an ultimatum to leave by noon, after which they re-locked the gates and cut off utility lines to the building.
Upon his rescue, the VC reported experiencing chest pain and a headache, stating that he required urgent medical assistance.
As he was escorted away from the campus, students were heard shouting 'Bhua! Bhua!' in protest.
caption:
Locked in for 30 hours with no utilities. The CUET VC has finally been rescued by district authorities.

Chattogram's deputy commissioner, superintendent of police, and the CUET proctor rescued Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Islam after he was confined for nearly 30 hours.

The situation began yesterday when demonstrating students locked the VC inside the administrative building around 12:30 PM, demanding his immediate resignation.

The confrontation flared up yesterday morning when the VC arrived on campus for the first time since his September 21 appointment, entering through the main gate by identifying himself as a teacher.

Students gathered in hundreds, chanting slogans and rejecting the new VC. They gave him an ultimatum to leave by noon, after which they re-locked the gates and cut off utility lines to the building.

Upon his rescue, the VC reported experiencing chest pain and a headache, stating that he required urgent medical assistance.

As he was escorted away from the campus, students were heard shouting 'Bhua! Bhua!' in protest.

headline_marked: Nobel laureate [[Prof Yunus harassed]] at JFK Airport by expatriate Bangladeshis
headline: Nobel laureate Prof Yunus harassed at JFK Airport by expatriate Bangladeshis
summary: Nobel Peace Prize winner Muhammad Yunus was confronted and verbally abused by a group of expatriate Bangladeshis upon his arrival at New York's JFK Airport. His entourage confirmed he was unharmed.
details: Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus faced harassment shortly after landing at John F Kennedy International Airport in New York. A video circulating on social media shows a group, including leaders of the New York Metropolitan Awami League and US Jubo League, confronting Yunus and shouting accusations.

During the confrontation, one individual shouted, “You killed a thousand people in Bangladesh. He killed a thousand police in my country. He destroyed the democracy in my country….” Yunus was then wheeled back into the terminal by his entourage.

Lamiya Morshed, an executive director at the Yunus Centre and a member of Yunus's entourage, confirmed that the Nobel laureate suffered no harm during the incident. She stated on Facebook, "He is absolutely fine."
Morshed described the incident as exposing "extreme savagery and pettiness" but reiterated that it caused no harm to Yunus. She also expressed gratitude for the messages of support received.

The incident has drawn condemnation from various quarters, with Jamaat leader Taher and others calling for an end to such behavior. The Bangladeshi government has also stated it will take action against those involved in the harassment.
